title: The Metaphor Stretch — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of The Metaphor Stretch's rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: two walks on the Crystal Synthesizer's own engine, ported from its Python, that end on measurements — the beating and the sweep pulled apart to ask which part of the sound is the crystal, and the four Decision Points taken in the lesson's order until a fifth, unnamed choice turns up — beside the crystal-rings strikes that put the decay rate to physics. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

verdicts.why: Evidence against Decision Point 3's 'does not specify the rate': a rate from measured line widths beside one chosen by taste. Caption checked against check_rings.py and linewidths.json (5.5 s ÷ (1 + 0.15 k), A2, three widths measured); tracked.

pieces.title: the taste decay, then the physics ring · crystal-rings, 2026-10-14
pieces.caption: **Decision Point 3, decided two ways.** Seven minerals at A2, in turn: diamond, fluorite, emerald, ruby, amethyst, topaz, labradorite. Each plays the summer proof's strike first, every mineral given the same 5.5-second ring shortened by mode number, a rate chosen by taste; then the crystal-rings resonator bank, each mode's ring time taken from the mineral's Raman line width (Q = line position ÷ width, τ = Q ÷ πf). Diamond stays a bell; the rest turn to knocks. Only three of the widths are measured values; the rest are estimates.

pieces.title: four choices, one crystal · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **The four Decision Points as the lesson the Forward Vectors ask for, then a test of the count.** Resolution first, the most audible; then the Anchor, three crystals landing three ways; then the Decay, with exponent 1 marked as what one measured Q gives; then the Fidelity Claim's three paths as three labelled renders, discrete, continuous, and the two separated. Last, with all four held still, the size of the grid the code computes its crystal on, its verdict computed from what the grids measure: under lowest mode the cubic crystal's top moves from 1.1 to 9.1 kHz (and drops to 6.5 at 77 cells, where the code's 0.012 floor bites), under zone boundary the floor moves, and under centroid the grid moves nothing and the anchor's hidden choice is its 88 Hz cut, 17 to 21 % of the modes. Each anchor hides a different choice. The engine renders the instrument's Python sample for sample.

pieces.title: which part is the crystal? · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Is the beating the crystal or the rendering, and is the sweep?** One struck partial, dying faster the higher it sits; two neighbours, whose beats are their gap in hertz; the whole crystal at 8 to 300 partials, each band's level drawn so the beating shows as ripple; and last five renders that pull the two apart. At the code's lowest-mode anchor, N = 8 has no beating at all and the brightness still falls by half over three seconds; with the decay exponent at 0 the beating at N = 300 is unchanged and the brightness does not fall. The sweep is the decay's, Decision Point 3; the beating is this engine's bins', and rides on it. Under the centroid anchor the crystal sits between 88 and 160 Hz and even N = 8 beats, at 7 to 12 a second. Noise per bin keeps the ripple as deep and loses its regularity. Measured on the instrument's own engine, in three crystals.
pieces.near: At Decision Point 2, an interesting case arises

offers.what: Decision Point 2 says N runs 'from 8 (bell-like instrument, discrete modes, audible beating) to 300+ (dense texture approaching the continuous DOS)'. Whether N = 8 beats depends on the anchor. At the code's lowest-mode anchor (and at zone boundary, which gives the same cents) neighbours at N = 8 sit 818 ¢ apart (cubic), 894 (orthorhombic), 773 (triclinic): no slow beating, ripple 0.2 to 0.4 dB. Beating arrives near N = 24 to 32 and is too fast to count through the middle (151 to 183 Hz near 1 kHz at N = 24, 37 to 42 at N = 100); at N = 300 it slows to 12.0 to 13.9 a second near 1 kHz and loses regularity (0.42 to 0.57), while noise per bin is as deep and irregular (0.10 to 0.13). Under the centroid anchor the whole crystal lands between 88 and 160 Hz, and N = 8 puts neighbours 133 ¢ apart, 7 to 12 Hz: slow, countable beating. Proposed: 'N ranges from 8 (bell-like, discrete modes) to 300+ (slow beating that loses its regularity, approaching the texture of the continuous DOS); how close neighbours sit at a given N depends on how wide the anchor spreads the crystal, so at the default lowest-mode anchor N = 8 does not beat, and under centroid it does.' The challenger's read, which this offer adopts: Resolution and Anchor are coupled. The code's DP2 comment ('Low N (8–20) → … Audible beating') holds only under centroid.

Narrow, not a reversal. The page already names the cause ('high modes do decay first'); what blurs it is 'the direction of the effect', which reads as if the sweep belonged to the beating. Measured on crystal_synth.py (maker's port and challenger's Python agree): with the decay law and no beating (N = 8, lowest mode) the centroid falls from 0.15 to 3 s by 47 % (cubic), 95 % (orthorhombic), 94 % (triclinic); with the exponent at 0 it falls 0.0 % while the N = 300 beating is unchanged. Under the centroid anchor at N = 300 the beating pushes the centroid up 48 to 63 % over 3 s, with or without the decay law: the beating has no direction of its own. Proposed for that one phrase: 'the sweep is the decay's and sounds with no beating at all; the beating is honest only in that it rides it.' The beat rates are confirmed as set by the bins (and the grid), not the lattice, in this engine.

'Four stretch points were formally identified.' Each anchor hides a choice the four don't name. Under lowest mode and zone boundary it is the grid the code computes on (dos_cubic(n=40), dos_triclinic(n=28)): the softest phonon goes to 0 Hz as k → 0, so 'the softest acoustic phonon' means nothing until a finite grid picks it. Under lowest mode the floor stays on 110 Hz and the cubic top runs 1097, 2307, 4732, 6776, 8334 Hz at 10, 20, 40, 80, 120 cells (spread ≈ 1.1 × n up to 76 cells; 9.1 kHz at 76, then 6.5 kHz at 77, where the 0.012 floor drops the softest mode); under zone boundary the floor runs 1003, 232, 132 Hz at 10, 40, 120. Under centroid the grid moves nothing (88 to 160 Hz at every grid), and the live hidden choice is the 88 Hz cut, which removes 17.5 / 21.2 / 19.5 % of the modes (cubic / orthorhombic / triclinic). Proposed: name these as hidden parts of the Frequency Anchor rather than a fifth category, and note that the code's DP1 comment, 'the spread is determined by physics', is the grid's doing.

From reading, not from a piece: Decision Point 3 says the physics 'does not specify the rate'. The crystal-rings build (Projects/Crystal Synthesizer/crystal-rings/README.md, 2026-10-14) takes the rate from a measured Raman line width, Q = line position ÷ width and τ = Q ÷ πf, which is a decay exponent of exactly 1 at that Q; its tail fits land within 0.1 to 2.2 % of Q ÷ πf (ring-findings.json). Only diamond's, amethyst's and fluorite's widths are measured (fluorite's from a powder; amethyst's from a search summary); the others are estimates, and one Q is given to every mode. Proposed: 'The physics guarantees the direction. Where a line width has been measured it can give the rate too, as the crystal-rings build does; what stays the designer's is giving every mode one width, and the exponent wherever no width is known.'
